title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Mercury?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Mercury at noon? The closest planet to the Sun is not the hottest.
In daylight the ground reaches about four hundred and thirty degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead.
There is almost no air, only a thin haze, so nothing holds that heat. At night it falls to minus one hundred and eighty.
The Sun would look more than three times bigger than from Earth, and sunlight would be up to seven times brighter.
A year on Mercury is only eighty-eight Earth days, but one sunrise to the next takes one hundred and seventy-six.
The only comfortable place is deep inside shadowed craters at the poles, where frost may be hiding in permanent dark.

description:
What if you stood on the surface of Mercury?
Day hits 430 degrees Celsius, night drops to minus 180, and the safest place may be a frozen crater at the pole.
What should we run through next?
